title: Microsoft 365 Family subscribers will finally be able to share AI benefits
summary:
Microsoft bundled its AI-powered Office features into Microsoft 365 Personal and Family subscriptions last year, but it only allowed the primary account holder to access the AI benefits.
Now, Microsoft is about to let Microsoft 365 Family and Premium subscribers share Copilot and AI usage features, alongside access to Office apps and OneDrive storage, with up to five other people on a plan.
In an email to Microsoft 365 Family and Premium subscribers seen by The Verge, Microsoft outlines the changes that are coming to subscription plans over the coming months:AI for everyone on your plan: Share your Copilot benefits and AI usage with other members on your plan.
More flexible AI usage: Your individual AI feature limits will shift to a single AI usage allowance that you can apply to the advanced AI features you use most.
The “more flexible AI usage” change could mean that some subscribers end up paying more for AI usage, depending on how they’re using Copilot.

title: Book Publishers Are Quietly Using More AI. Staff Are Revolting
summary:
In headline after headline this year, American book publishers have appeared to be fighting back against generative AI, from suing Google for copyright infringement to canceling books by authors suspected of using LLMs.
But behind the scenes, at least three of the Big Five US book publishers—HarperCollins, Simon & Schuster, and Hachette—have been quietly incorporating AI tools into their publishing processes without public disclosures or author consent.
“Every single imprint has a story of someone very esteemed who had a book canceled because of blatant AI use” without ever making the news, one editor says.
Dozens of junior- and senior-level staff were then “voluntold” to become “AI Champions” and were tasked with discovering use cases in monthly brainstorming sessions with staff across the company.
But according to workers at HarperCollins, Simon & Schuster, and Hachette, one of the most common use cases for LLMs so far is generating publicity copy.

title: An experiment to glimpse the future Amazon — in pictures
summary:
From above, the patch of Amazon forest looks like an immense tapestry, full of shades and textures.
Rising from the green landscape are metal towers that form six rings above the canopy.
It is here, 80 kilometres north of Manaus in Brazil, that David Lapola, a climatologist at the State University of Campinas (Unicamp) in Brazil, and his team come to listen to the forest breathe.
The rings mark the site of the Amazon Free-Air CO 2 Enrichment Experiment (AmazonFACE), which is set to launch in the next few months.
The decade-long project will test how the forest might respond to atmospheres of the future, when rising carbon dioxide levels are likely to affect plant growth and carbon storage.

title: UK can’t rely on AI that could be switched off, Turing chief tells Guardian
summary:
The UK must not depend on foreign AI that could be cut off at short notice, the new head of the Alan Turing Institute has said.
“We shouldn’t depend solely on systems we can’t inspect or control, or that could be restricted or even switched off,” Williamson said.
He pointed to defence, national security, critical infrastructure and healthcare as areas where AI is now built in.
Williamson said the UK should have some AI it does not need anyone’s permission to use.
The institute cannot match the budgets of big AI labs, he added, but it could build smaller, nationally owned models for start-ups.
